method: Computed the supplied PDF's SHA-256 hash and byte size and compared the hash against every published public asset and evidence catalog.
Opened all nine pages, extracted the complete embedded text and confirmed that every page is readable and the first page is not blank.
Rendered and visually inspected evidentiary pages 6 through 8, which contain the paid-treatment discussion, collection and hauling explanation, motion number, permit number and vote.
Compared the official minutes with the existing 102-page November 20 council packet and the separate unsigned proposed-resolution attachment; all three are distinct records.
Added the official minutes once, linked the source to a dated timeline event and rechecked the evidence request queue without closing unsupported requirements.

addedRecord.canonicalName: November 20, 2017 Cadillac City Council Meeting Minutes.pdf

existingCouncilPacket.relationship: Same meeting context, but a distinct pre-meeting council packet rather than the official minutes.

existingProposedResolution.relationship: Distinct unsigned proposed-resolution attachment. The official minutes establish that motion 2017-232 was unanimously approved.

verifiedFindings: Pages 6 and 7 record City Manager Marcus Peccia's statements that Cadillac benefited from the landfill company depositing leachate at the WWTP, was paid to treat it, would lose that revenue to a deep injection well, and was responsible for treating the waste and discharging the treated water.

Pages 7 and 8 record Utilities Director Jeff Dietlin's explanation that rainwater and liquid from garbage were collected at the bottom of landfill cells, pumped to a tank and hauled to Cadillac's WWTP.
Page 8 records motion 2017-232 opposing draft permit MI-165-1I-0002 and states that the motion was unanimously approved.

queueResolution.reason: The official minutes establish the paid landfill-to-WWTP treatment relationship and the Council's action, but they do not provide an executed 2009 agreement package, load-by-load manifests, invoices, an exact final delivery date, PFAS analytical results or source-to-receptor migration proof.
